evidence:
Source: Morwani, Edelman, Oncescu, Zhao, Kakade, "Feature emergence via margin maximization: case studies in algebraic tasks", ICLR 2024 Spotlight, arXiv:2311.07568v2. I fetched the HTML and the abs page and grepped them.

What they prove:
- Sec 3.2 "Multi-Class Classification" defines the class-weighted margin for any weighting tau(x,y) over the wrong labels: g'(theta,x,y) = f(theta,x)[y] - sum_{y' != y} tau(x,y)[y'] f(theta,x)[y'].
- Same section, verbatim: "Note that g'(theta,x,y) >= g(theta,x,y) as g' replaces the max by a weighted sum."
- q* is uniform on the data (Sec 3.3, step 1).
- App. F.1 (proof of Thm 7) defines, for a single neuron, eta_{u,v,w}(delta) := E_{a,b}[(u(a)+v(b))^2 w(a+b-delta)]. It maximises eta(0) - E_{delta != 0} eta(delta) (Eq. 4) with uniform tau(a,b)[c'] = 1/(p-1).

Why our lemma is a specialisation: lem:avg is exactly Morwani's inequality with q uniform on D_p and tau set to the point mass on y(x)-delta, summed over neurons (eta_theta = sum_i eta_{omega_i} by linearity).

The only difference: we use a point-mass tau at each offset instead of a uniform tau. That gives one inequality per delta, which the later coverage min over delta needs. The step is trivial and adds nothing as a result.

The paper's current wording already credits Morwani appropriately. The bib entry is correct: title, authors and ICLR 2024 confirmed.

recommended_citations.why: Supports approach.tex line 7 ('minimum margin is at most any averaged class-weighted margin'). Sec 3.2 proves g' >= g for any class weighting tau. App. F.1 defines the single-neuron eta_{u,v,w}(delta), of which our eta_theta is the network-level sum. Already cited; only the section pointers need tightening.

recommended_change:
Two small fixes to the pointers. The lemma itself needs no change.

- approach.tex l.7: change "\citep[Section~3]{morwani2024feature}" to "\citep[Section~3.2]{morwani2024feature}".
- approach.tex l.11: change "the quantity $\eta_{u,v,w}(\delta)$ of \citet{morwani2024feature}" to "the quantity $\eta_{u,v,w}(\delta)$ of \citet[Appendix~F.1]{morwani2024feature}".

Optional clause after the lemma: "Morwani et al. use a uniform weighting over wrong labels, i.e. the average of this bound over $\delta$; keeping each $\delta$ separately is what allows the minimum over offsets in Lemma~\ref{lem:phase}." Do not present lem:avg as a contribution.
